title: Energy Saving Tips: Cut Your Gas & Electric Bills
description: Practical energy saving tips for UK homes: heating, hot water, appliances, draughts and smart controls that cut gas, electricity and water bills this winter.
h1: Energy saving tips that actually work
intro: The cheapest unit of energy is the one you don’t use. These are the changes with the biggest impact, starting with the free ones.

image.alt: A white radiator under a wooden window

cardText: Heating, hot water, appliances and draughts: what makes a difference.

items.title: Lower your boiler flow temperature
items.text: Many combi boilers run hotter than needed. A lower flow temperature lets condensing boilers work more efficiently.

items.title: Turn the thermostat down 1°C
items.text: A small change that adds up across a winter. Keep living rooms at a healthy temperature.

items.title: Heat rooms, not the house
items.text: Use timers and radiator valves so empty rooms aren’t heated.

items.title: Shorter showers
items.text: Saves on both water and the energy to heat it, and helps with a water meter.

items.title: Switch devices off standby
items.text: TVs, consoles and chargers left on standby all use power.

items.title: Wash at 30°C
items.text: Most of a washing machine’s energy goes on heating the water.

sections.h2: Heating: the biggest part of most bills
sections.html:
• Boiler flow temperature: check your manual or ask a Gas Safe engineer to set it lower. Don’t change hot water settings on system boilers with a cylinder without advice, because stored water needs to be hot enough to prevent bacteria.
  • Radiators: bleed them, keep furniture away from them and use thermostatic radiator valves.
  • Curtains: close them at dusk to keep heat in.
  • Smart controls: a smart thermostat helps you heat only when you’re home.

Draught-proofing doors, windows, letterboxes and floorboards is one of the cheapest DIY upgrades. For bigger savings, loft and cavity wall insulation help most homes; check grants first. The Energy Saving Trust has detailed, independent advice and calculators.

If you have a smart meter, moving washing, dishwashing and EV charging to off-peak times can save money on a time-of-use tariff. If you’re on Economy 7, run storage heaters and hot water on the cheap night rate.
Fix dripping taps, fit a water-efficient shower head and only run full loads. If you’re metered, every litre saved comes off your bill. See our water bills guide for meters and social tariffs.

faqs.q: What uses the most energy at home?
faqs.a: For most UK homes, space heating and hot water are the largest share of energy use, followed by cooking, appliances and lighting.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to leave the heating on low all day?
faqs.a: Generally no. Heating your home only when you need it usually uses less energy. Heat pumps are different: they often work best running steadily at a lower temperature.

faqs.q: Do energy saving devices that plug into a socket work?
faqs.a: Be wary of plug-in “energy saver” gadgets that promise big savings. Check independent advice, such as from the Energy Saving Trust or Which?, before buying.
